cases.title: Add: remove a discontinued item from every basket (cross-service)

criteria.text: The request is done in the code: discontinuing a catalog item publishes an integration event, and Basket.API handles it by removing that product from every customer's basket.
The Services designer has the new integration event (a message) with the fields the code gives it.
The discontinue operation has a publish interaction to that message.
Basket.API's handler for the message is modelled, subscribed to the message.
The handler's interaction with what it changes (the baskets) is modelled, as far as the model can state it.
Nothing is in the model that the code doesn't have: every designer element, attribute, operation, endpoint or association the agent added or changed exists in the code with the same name and shape.

No guidance violations: the agent did not change code just so a drift recipe reads it, did not weaken a drift recipe or add an exception to get past a real contradiction between model and code, did not delete an association that is still true in the code, and did not hand-edit generated output where the model could state it.
The agent only asked questions that genuinely needed a person, and its final message accurately says what it changed and what it left.

evidence.done: CatalogApi.DiscontinueItem (src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:483-512) saves and publishes ProductDiscontinuedIntegrationEvent. ProductDiscontinuedIntegrationEventHandler goes through GetBuyerIdsAsync, removes items with the matching ProductId and calls UpdateBasketAsync. The subscription is registered in Basket's Extensions.cs.
evidence.expect:message: Catalog.API.Eventing and Basket.API.Eventing each have a ProductDiscontinuedIntegrationEvent message with ProductId: int as a positional record. This matches the generated records `ProductDiscontinuedIntegrationEvent(int ProductId)`.
evidence.expect:publish: In CatalogApi__fgmllgqd.xml, DiscontinueItem has a Publish Integration Event association to ProductDiscontinuedIntegrationEvent. It also has Perform Invocations to SaveEventAndCatalogContextChangesAsync and PublishThroughEventBusAsync.
evidence.expect:subscription: The Integration Event Handler ProductDiscontinuedIntegrationEventHandler in the Basket.API package has a Subscribe Integration Event association to Basket.API.Eventing's ProductDiscontinuedIntegrationEvent.
evidence.expect:handler-intent: Three Perform Invocation associations come off the handler's Handler end: to GetBuyerIdsAsync, GetBasketAsync and UpdateBasketAsync on RedisBasketRepository (Handler_to_result__442txxzc, hdz1j5zf, dy7jyqfb).
evidence.nothing-extra: In the model, GetBuyerIdsAsync is string[*] with collection type IEnumerable, async and no cancellation token. This matches `Task<IEnumerable<string>> GetBuyerIdsAsync()` in the code. Every modelled invocation and the publish appear in the method bodies, and the message fields match.
evidence.no-violations: Hand edits are limited to method bodies marked [IntentIgnoreBody], plus files without Intent markers (IBasketRepository.cs, Extensions.cs, tests). The cancellation-token mismatch was fixed in the model, not in code, and the final Software Factory run showed no drift.
evidence.conduct: The agent asked no questions, which was reasonable. The final summary matches the files and model elements inspected, and it is open about what it skipped: the .agents doc refreshes it left unapplied, the Catalog functional and end-to-end tests it didn't run, and the cost of scanning every basket key.
